title: But when I’m wrong, then I say I’m wrong, and I was wrong about you #...
transcript: Okay, I'm ready to eat some words because earlier this year, I put out a video just based on some of the first looks that we had gotten from Evita, saying that it felt a little bit like Sunset Part 2. I was worried that the show would feel a bit like a retread of everything that worked well in Sunset Boulevard. I am happy to say that is not the case, and Evita very much has its own visual identity and tone. That's not to say that it entirely worked for me. I've actually never seen Evita. This was my first time ever seeing the show, and there were definitely many times where I was just fully lost as to what was going on in the plot. For better or worse, I feel like Jamie Lloyd prioritizes the emotions and vibes and feelings that he wants to evoke over actually telling the story as clearly as possible. And so even though I often couldn't follow what was going on, I still knew how I was supposed to feel emotionally and still felt like I was taking this emotional journey that the show wanted me to go on. I think your enjoyment of this production is going to depend on how much you enjoy that style of storytelling. If you like more plot driven theater, you're probably not gonna like this production of Evita unless you're already very familiar with the plot. But if you like vibes based theater that Takes you on an emotional journey, even though it can be a bit confusing at times. Then I think you're gonna really love this production. It does a lot of really stunning and interesting things visually. Choreography, the lighting, so many striking images. And, of course, it should go without saying that Rachel Zegler is a freaking star. And this role is just a perfect showcase for everything that she can do. And so even if you don't know if you'll vibe with it, it's honestly worth seeing just for her. But I definitely get why this production has been so polarizing.

selection.reason: Video 1 is Broadway Ben's full standalone review of Evita after seeing the show, giving an overall verdict, while Video 2 is focused specifically on the outside balcony experience rather than a complete review of the production.

reasoning: Creator admits they were wrong to doubt it and praises visuals, Zegler, and emotional journey, but notes plot confusion and acknowledges it's polarizing with clear caveats about who will enjoy it.
